skill.name: ai-video-generation
skill.description: Generate AI video prompts and run inference.sh belt CLI workflows for text-to-video, image-to-video, avatars, lipsync, editing, upscaling, foley, and media merging.
skill.summary: Run inference.sh video models from Claude, Codex, or Claude Code using belt CLI examples.
skill.author: skills-shell

security_audit.summary: The static backtick detections are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, inline commands, and model identifiers. No Ruby or shell command-substitution source is present. The real risks are external CLI dependency and hosted video processing of prompts, media URLs, likenesses, and voices.

remediation.issue: External CLI dependency is required for core use.
remediation.suggestion: Document the exact trusted install source, version expectations, and verification steps for the belt CLI before users run commands.

remediation.issue: Prompts and media URLs may leave the user workspace.
remediation.suggestion: Add explicit privacy warnings before examples that submit images, voices, likenesses, videos, or confidential prompts to hosted models.

remediation.issue: Generation commands may consume paid service credits.
remediation.suggestion: Require user confirmation for model, duration, resolution, and cost-sensitive options before running belt app commands.

semantic_findings.title: Unverified Third-Party CLI Dependency
semantic_findings.description: The skill directs users to install the belt CLI skill and follow remote install instructions before use. A community skill depending on an external CLI and remote setup path creates supply-chain exposure.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: SKILL.md explicitly instructs users to install the belt CLI skill and links to remote installation instructions. This is a clear dependency risk, although no malicious install behavior is shown in this file.

semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The file describes inference.sh CLI use and shows commands with image_url, audio_url, video, and video_url inputs. The risk is inherent to the documented hosted AI workflow, not hidden behavior.

content.value_statement: AI video workflows can be hard to map across many model providers. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code structured belt CLI examples for common video generation tasks.
actual_capabilities: Lists text-to-video models such as Veo, Seedance, HappyHorse, Wan, and Grok.
Provides belt CLI examples for image-to-video and reference-to-video workflows.
Shows avatar and lipsync commands for OmniHuman, Fabric, and PixVerse models.
Includes examples for video editing, foley sound, upscaling, and media merging.
Links users to inference.sh documentation for running apps and streaming results.
limitations: Requires the inference.sh belt CLI and an authenticated account.
Actual model availability, pricing, and output quality depend on inference.sh services.
User media URLs, prompts, voices, and likenesses may be sent to third-party model providers.
The skill is documentation-focused and does not validate inputs before commands run.

use_cases.title: Create Social Video Concepts
use_cases.description: Generate short text-to-video clips for campaigns, posts, and visual experiments.

use_cases.title: Animate Product Images
use_cases.description: Turn product stills or reference images into short motion clips with model-specific commands.

use_cases.title: Prototype Avatar Videos
use_cases.description: Test avatar, lipsync, and narration workflows before building a larger content pipeline.

prompt_templates.title: Beginner Text-to-Video
prompt_templates.scenario: Create a first simple clip from a written idea.
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate a short AI video of a calm forest sunrise. Use the fastest suitable model and explain what each input controls.

prompt_templates.title: Image Animation
prompt_templates.scenario: Animate a still image from a user-provided URL.
prompt_templates.prompt: Animate this image into a five second video with gentle camera movement. Choose an image-to-video model and include privacy cautions before running it.

prompt_templates.title: Avatar Lipsync Workflow
prompt_templates.scenario: Build a talking-head video from portrait and audio URLs.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an avatar video from my portrait and narration audio. Compare OmniHuman, Fabric, and PixVerse options before selecting a command.

prompt_templates.title: Advanced Video Pipeline
prompt_templates.scenario: Combine generation, sound effects, upscaling, and merging.
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a complete AI video pipeline with generated scenes, foley audio, upscaling, and transitions. Ask for confirmation before any paid or external call.

output_examples.input: A user asks for a five second product teaser from a still image.
output_examples.output: The assistant recommends an image-to-video model, asks for the image URL, warns that the image will leave the workspace, and prepares the belt command.

output_examples.input: A creator wants a talking-head video from a portrait and narration track.
output_examples.output: The assistant compares avatar and lipsync models, requests consent for likeness and voice processing, then outlines the selected workflow.

output_examples.input: A team has several silent clips and wants a finished social video.
output_examples.output: The assistant proposes foley sound, upscaling, and merging steps, with checkpoints before each external service call.

best_practices: Confirm model choice, cost, duration, and resolution before running belt commands.
Use only media URLs that the user owns or has permission to process.
Warn users when prompts, images, audio, or videos will be sent to external services.
anti_patterns: Do not upload private likenesses, voices, or unreleased media without explicit consent.
Do not run paid generation commands before the user approves the final inputs.
Do not assume every listed model is available in every inference.sh account or region.

faq.question: Does this skill generate video locally?
faq.answer: No. It uses the inference.sh belt CLI to call hosted AI video models.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Can it turn an image into a video?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill includes image-to-video examples for Wan, Seedance, HappyHorse, and related models.

faq.question: Can it make avatar or lipsync videos?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes examples for OmniHuman, Fabric, and PixVerse lipsync workflows.

faq.question: What should users check before running commands?
faq.answer: Users should confirm account access, pricing, media rights, privacy expectations, and final inputs.

faq.question: Are external services involved?
faq.answer: Yes. Commands call inference.sh and may send prompts or media URLs to hosted model providers.
